thread:
Anya: Heads-up — I'm bringing up sable-embed-1b (ONNX int8, per-channel) on embed-staging for onboarding. Running our standard recall/clustering/umap/eval harness against holdout-250k. Early results show a noticeable recall@10 drop vs prod-embed-small (cosine). Posting quick summary and logs below.

David: Can you paste the eval command, dataset split, and index config so I can repro locally? Which metric (cosine/dot)?

Anya: Sure — holdout-250k same as bench, metric=cosine, FAISS HNSW with efConstruction=200, efSearch=128. Eval command I ran: 

```\npython eval/compare_embeddings.py \\\n  --model sable-embed-1b:onnx-int8 \\\n  --baseline prod-embed-small:fp16 \\\n  --holdout datasets/holdout-250k.jsonl \\\n  --index hnsw --hnsw-efc 200 --hnsw-efs 128 \\\n  --metric cosine \\\n  --normalize True \\\n  --out artifacts/sable_onboard/1723345566/\n```

embed-ci-bot: CI summary (full run finished): recall@1 baseline=0.612 -> sable=0.587 (-0.025), recall@5 0.818 -> 0.792 (-0.026), recall@10 0.892 -> 0.855 (-0.037). Silhouette (kmeans k=50) baseline=0.180 -> sable=0.150. UMAP preview: clusters slightly closer, fewer well-separated islands. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/example/artifacts/1723345566 (perf/logs/umap.png)

Sanjeev: Int8 quant can shift vector norms and change angular geometry. Were embeddings L2-normalized before indexing? We sometimes see big gains by normalizing pre-quant and using dot after normalization. Also try per-channel symmetric quant vs per-tensor.

Lina: I pushed a quick repro script and a small sweep (int8 vs fp16, normalize True/False). Run like: 

```\npython eval/repro_quick.py --model sable-embed-1b --quant int8 fp16 --normalize True --subset 50k --index hnsw\n```

Quick-run results (50k subset): int8 + normalize: recall@10 delta vs fp16 = -0.008 (much smaller), int8 without normalize = -0.034. So normalization reduces the gap a lot on the subset.

David: Good find. Also check ID flip rate (nearest neighbor identity flips). If many flips at @1 that suggests topology change, not just magnitude.

Anya: ID flip @1 ~2.3% on full 250k holdout, higher for queries with longer contexts. Per-channel quant seems slightly better than per-tensor. I'm scheduling a full per-channel symmetric vs per-tensor run + normalization tonight, plus one run switching metric to dot with pre-normalized vectors to see if that recovers. If per-channel + normalize still bad, we'll try 4-bit dynamic and a calibration pass on holdout.

Sanjeev: Also dump cosine histograms and centroid shifts between baseline and sable — that'll show global shifts. If centroids moved, a simple global rescale or bias-correction might help.

Lina: Added a small notebook to artifacts that plots cosine distribution and kNN distance CDFs: artifacts/sable_onboard/1723345566/diagnostics.ipynb

embed-ci-bot: Noted: scheduled re-runs (per-channel-symmetric + normalize) at 2024-05-11T02:00Z. Will post results when done.

David: Nice iterative plan. If re-run still unhappy, we should also benchmark downstream clustering/RAG retrieval quality (not just recall) — e.g., rerank delta on our eval prompts.

Anya: Agreed — next step is to run a small RAG eval and a reranker pass after quant variants. I'll post updated numbers + a short write-up tomorrow AM. Thanks for the quick checks :thumbsup:
